note: The five open dominant 7th shapes: E7 and A7 as E and A with one finger let go, D7, G7 and B7 new, then strummed in time and into the chords they lead to. The open shapes are the lesson, so only the tempo moves (60 to 80 bpm); the why says what makes each shape easy, and the second block names its goal with "Practice until".

exercise.title: Open 7th chords: E7, A7, D7, G7, B7
exercise.why: E7 and A7 are E and A with one fretted string let go, so each 7th chord starts from a shape your hand already knows.

cells.heading: E to E7, A to A7

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear it, then fret each chord as shown. Change from E to E7 and back, then from A to A7 and back.
In each 7th chord, one string that was fretted now rings open: pick the strings one at a time to check that it rings.

Press a chord box below to hear it, then fret D7, G7 and B7 as shown. B7 takes four fingers, so build it slowly, one finger at a time.
Practice until each shape lands with all its fingers at once.

cells.heading: A7, D7 and E7 in time

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down on every beat.
If a change comes late, keep your strumming hand going and catch the next beat 1.

Press Play below to start the metronome and strum down on every beat: G7 to C, then B7 to Em.
Listen for the pull from each 7th chord into the chord after it.
